body.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_N\), the support-preserving continuum \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\) can be chosen so that its local log-likelihood quadratic for a ratio displacement \(h\) is comparable, with constants depending only on the class constants, to \(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). Hence the squared inverse local testing radius at \(\theta_T\) is comparable to \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\), and the necessity geometry is the same support-constrained quadratic form \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\) as the exact pooled efficiency bound.
body.justification: This makes the collection program both an attainable score variance and an all-procedure information modulus.
body.gap: Su et al. optimize regular source weights, while Cai and Low study an abstract modulus; neither derives this causal support-constrained observed-law modulus.
body.consumer: Trial collections can be ranked even when no single trial covers the target.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 I_x(\theta)=\sum_{s:x\in\mathcal H_s}
       \frac{n_sp_s(x)}{q_{sx}(\theta)}.
\]
The denominators are positive by residual-variance regularity. Minimizing independently at each cell, the Lagrange equations give
\[
 a_{sx}^{\star}(\theta)
 =p_T(x)\frac{n_sp_s(x)/q_{sx}(\theta)}{I_x(\theta)},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
 =\sum_x\frac{p_T(x)^2}{I_x(\theta)}.
\]
These formulas also cover cells having a single source.

Let \(b_x\) be the common perturbation of the residual contrast at cell \(x\). In a supported source-cell, the mean-zero conditional score
\[
 \frac{b_x}{q_{sx}(\theta)}
 \left[
  \frac{Z}{e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx1}(\theta)\}
  -\frac{1-Z}{1-e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx0}(\theta)\}
 \right]
\]
has derivative \(b_x\) for the arm contrast and conditional squared norm \(b_x^2/q_{sx}(\theta)\). Exponential tilting on the existing support, with the compensating latent-type tilt in the local-collection construction, preserves randomization, exclusion, monotonicity, source support, and the common contrast. Boundedness and the overlap and mass bounds make the Taylor expansion of each conditional log normalizer uniform. The product log-likelihood quadratic is therefore
\[
 \frac12\sum_x I_x(\theta)b_x^2+o(1).
\]
For a ratio displacement \(h\) at \(\theta_T\), the constraint is \(\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh\). Another Lagrange calculation yields
\[
 b_x^{\star}
 =-\frac{\mu_Dh}{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}
   \frac{p_T(x)}{I_x(\theta_T)}
\]
and
\[
 \min_{\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh}\sum_xI_x(\theta_T)b_x^2
 =\frac{\mu_D^2h^2}{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}
 =h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P).
\]
The bounded compensations can change the quadratic only by constants depending on \(e_0,p_0,\rho_0,v_0,K\), and \(|\mathcal X|\); the bounds are uniform because these quantities are fixed. Thus the squared inverse testing radius is comparable to \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). The calculation is also the dual of the exact allocation program, proving that the local necessity geometry is \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\), including at allocation-face changes.
